clue.text: Last month container held one crustacean

indicators.note: the pair of pieces before it is said to have held something, so the next piece goes inside them

parts.note: December, the last month of the year, is abbreviated DEC
a pod is a container, as for peas or seeds
one is the indefinite article a

explanation.surface: A crab arrived in a container at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' reads as a count of crustaceans; here it is just the article, and 'held' tucks it between the month and the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A decapod is a ten-legged crustacean such as a crab, lobster or shrimp.

clue.text: Vessel off-course?

parts.note: a boat that has lost its course just floats along with the current, and the name of one kind of fishing boat says exactly that

explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a fishing boat using drift nets, and also anything carried along aimlessly by the current.

clue.text: Like those watching TV in prison?

definitions.text: Like those watching TV in prison?

parts.words: Like those watching TV in prison?
parts.note: inmates watching television cannot leave, so they are viewers held in place in a literal sense

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a crowd of listeners or viewers who cannot get away; prisoners are literally held captive.

clue.text: Bet on the Irish pound

definitions.meaning: to place a bet, a gamble
the old Irish currency unit before the euro was known as the ...

explanation.surface: Gambling on the old Irish currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Punting is informal for wagering, and the Irish pound's Irish-language name was the punt.

clue.text: Does family have leather?

parts.note: kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A question whether a household owns any leather goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' reads as a verb starting a question; it is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is soft leather made from the hide of a female deer, or a lamb or sheep.

clue.text: Depending on free oxygen for singular rhythmic exercise

indicators.note: singular asks for the one-thing form of the plural-looking exercise word, so its final plural letter is dropped

parts.note: aerobics is rhythmic exercise done to music

explanation.surface: A breathing fitness class for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' drops the S from AEROBICS, as if it were a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic organisms or processes need atmospheric oxygen to live or work.

clue.text: The liar's tale in five acts!

definitions.text: The liar's tale in five acts!

parts.words: The liar's tale in five acts!
parts.note: looks like a theatre play in five acts, but points to chapter five of the Acts of the Apostles, where a man lies about money and falls dead

explanation.walkthrough: 'five acts' suggests a stage play; it means Acts chapter 5 in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananias, in Acts 5, lied to the apostles about the price of his land and was struck dead; his name became a byword for a liar.

clue.text: Attack made by soldiers I had concluded

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers
I had is contracted to I'd

explanation.surface: A soldier reports that the troops' assault is over.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment; 'concluded' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack or assault on a place.

clue.text: Disclosing a dark secret?

parts.note: something in the dark is literally carried into brightness when it is revealed, so the idiom for revealing is read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means revealing or exposing something hidden; a dark thing is literally moved into brightness.

clue.text: Sob before taking round information on refrigerant

parts.note: to sob is to cry
O is round in shape
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A weeping technician learns about a cooling substance.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryogen is a substance used to produce very low temperatures, such as liquid nitrogen.

clue.text: I am to meditate using skill despite suffering weightlessness!

parts.note: I am is contracted to I'm
to ponder is to meditate, think deeply
ability is skill

explanation.surface: Someone vows to meditate skilfully even while floating unwilling in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Imponderable means having no measurable weight, so imponderability is the state of lacking weight.

clue.text: Beastly conclusion

parts.note: beastly sounds like 'horrible', but it means belonging to a beast: the end of an animal's body

explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hindmost appendage is its rear end, the creature's final part.

clue.text: Is ken moved by the flock of wild geese in flight?

definitions.text: flock of wild geese in flight

indicators.note: the letters of 'Is ken' are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's knowledge is stirred by migrating geese overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' reads as emotionally touched; it rearranges IS KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the collective noun for wild geese flying in formation.

clue.text: Excited a giant

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, paired with Magog in British folklore

explanation.surface: A huge creature is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giants of legend whose effigies stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, keen and thrilled.

clue.text: One is encouraged to take this card

definitions.text: One is encouraged to take this card

parts.words: One is encouraged to take this card
parts.note: to take courage is an idiom with this organ in it, and the organ is also a suit symbol on playing cards

explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is a card suit, and 'take heart' means be encouraged.

clue.text: Tinny? That's shrewd

parts.note: tinny suggests 'like a tin', and a tin is also called a can, so this word for shrewd looks as if it means can-like

explanation.definitionFit: Canny means astute or shrewd; read jokingly it suggests 'like a can', which is tinny.

clue.text: Doreen wandering round a famous school

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes round the next piece, enclosing it
the letters of the name Doreen wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl called Doreen strays about an old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges DOREEN into ROEDEN, and 'round' puts A inside it. ROEDEAN is a girls' boarding school near Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a well-known independent girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast.

clue.text: Order to be quiet given to lady on river

parts.note: sh is the command for silence
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman on a riverbank is told to hush.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.

clue.text: Levelled the scores? That's settled

definitions.meaning: to have made the scores equal, as in a match that is all square
paid off or sorted, as when an account or matter is resolved

explanation.surface: A team drew level, and so the matter was finished.
explanation.definitionFit: All square means level in a game, and to square a debt is to pay or settle it.

clue.text: Thus fabulous bird was held with egg in the wind

indicators.note: the bird piece was held within the word for thus, so it goes inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written
the roc is a giant mythical bird in the Arabian Nights
O is egg-shaped

explanation.surface: A mythical bird is caught along with its egg in a desert storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means mythical here, not marvellous; the giant bird is from the Arabian Nights, and 'was held' places it inside the Latin word for thus.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Skilful to include large company in shortfall

indicators.note: the word for skilful is made to include the company, which goes inside it

parts.note: deft means skilful, nimble
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a large British company

explanation.surface: A skilled manager takes on a big firm despite a cash gap.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a major British chemicals firm, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is the amount by which money or supply falls short.

clue.text: Watch the screen

definitions.meaning: to keep an eye on or observe something over time
a display unit for a computer or a TV studio

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep your eyes on the TV.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to observe; a monitor is also a display screen.

clue.text: Lady hurried in amid confusion

indicators.note: the word for hurried is put in the jumbled letters
confusion signals that the letters of amid are scrambled

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A woman rushes into a chaotic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' looks like a link word placing the lady among confusion, but it is the fodder that 'confusion' scrambles, with 'in' signalling the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a woman's name, the heroine of Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Passed on transmitted messages

definitions.meaning: handed along to the next person, as in a team race
sent signals on, as a radio station rebroadcasts

explanation.surface: Messages were sent on down the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to pass something along in stages, or to retransmit a broadcast.

clue.text: Destruction of most of old castle perhaps

indicators.note: most of means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: the remains of an old castle are its ruins, an example

explanation.surface: Most of an old fort has been destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last S from RUINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin means downfall or wreckage, total destruction.

clue.text: Inflamed with a strong passion

parts.note: fire is intense passion or ardour

explanation.surface: Someone is burning with ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire means burning, ablaze, literally or with emotion.

clue.text: Articles from two countries left on airline

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article, Spain being one of the countries
a is the English indefinite article, England being the other country

explanation.surface: Goods from abroad are left on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: EL is 'the' in Spanish and A is English. EL AL is Israel's national airline.
explanation.definitionFit: El Al is the national airline of Israel.

clue.text: In this place — hear, hear!

indicators.note: the repeated hear tells us the first word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: hear is a word whose sound matches the word for in this place

explanation.surface: A parliamentary cry of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear, hear!' is the cry of approval in the British Parliament; the second 'hear' says the first is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means at or in this spot or location.

clue.text: Violet takes nearly new plant

parts.note: Vi is a short form of the woman's name Violet

indicators.note: nearly means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A woman picks up a plant in almost mint condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts the W from NEW, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vine is a climbing or trailing plant, especially the grapevine.

clue.text: Prisoner going down before second half of July in a patronising manner

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
descending means going down

indicators.note: second half of means only the latter half of the word is used

explanation.surface: A convict heading downstairs in July adopts a superior air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of' takes LY from JULY.
explanation.definitionFit: Condescendingly means behaving with an air of superiority, talking down to others.

clue.text: Get stuffed!

parts.note: looks like a rude dismissal, but read literally it tells you to fill yourself with food

explanation.definitionFit: To eat to excess is literally to become stuffed full of food.

clue.text: Warned later about abridged edition

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of later are moved around

parts.note: ED is the shortened form of edition

explanation.surface: A notice came later about a shortened version of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerted means given a warning of danger, put on guard.
